claim: Despite the DMA requiring Apple to permit alternative app stores in the EU since March 2024, EU alternative-marketplace adoption remains below 3% as of 2025, indicating structural (multi-store) DMA remedies have had far less practical effect than anti-steering/external-payment-link remedies.
stance_target: DMA structural remedies (competing app stores) meaningfully erode Apple's commission base in the near term
quoted_support: Despite the DMA requiring Apple to allow alternative app stores in the EU since March 2024, EU alternative marketplace adoption rates remain below 3% as of 2025.

claim: Per Apple's own November 2025 analysis, 88% of EU developers pay no Apple commission at all and 75% are enrolled in the Small Business Program with reduced (15%) rates -- a self-reported figure suggesting the commissionable developer base in the EU is already concentrated in a minority of larger developers.
stance_target: Concentration of commissionable revenue among a small share of developers
scope_conditions: European Union, per Apple self-report, November 2025
quoted_support: 88% of EU developers pay no Apple commission at all, and 75% are enrolled in the Small Business Program with reduced rates, per Apple's own November 2025 analysis.
numbers: 88% of EU developers pay no commission
75% enrolled in Small Business Program (15% rate)
